function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick guide to help you find the perfect place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a nationwide service.

---

## 1️⃣ Local & Specialty Bakeries  
These are often the best places for fresh, custom‑made cakes.

| Platform / Service | What it offers | How to find them |
|--------------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Google Maps / Apple Maps** | Search “cake shop near me” or “custom cake” | Shows ratings, photos, hours, and contact info |
| **Yelp** | Reviews + photos | Filter by “Open Now,” “Delivery,” or “Takeout” |
| **Local Facebook Groups / Nextdoor** | Recommendations from neighbors | Ask for “best cake shop” or “custom cake delivery” |
| **Instagram** | Look at hashtags like #YourCityBakery or #CustomCake | Many shops post their latest creations |

> **Tip:** Call ahead to confirm they deliver to your address and ask about special dietary needs (gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free).

---

## 2️⃣ Online Delivery Platforms  
If you prefer a quick pick‑up or delivery without calling each shop:

| Platform | Coverage | Features |
|----------|----------|----------|
| **Uber Eats** | City‑wide | Browse local bakeries, see real‑time delivery status |
| **DoorDash** | City‑wide | Often has exclusive deals, “DashPass” subscription |
| **Postmates** | City‑wide | Good for last‑minute orders, “Postmates Unlimited” |
| **Instacart** | Grocery + specialty items | Some stores offer pre‑baked cakes; you can add other groceries |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Nationwide (in select cities) | Offers pre‑baked cakes from local vendors |

> **Pro tip:** Check the “Specialty Food” section on these apps—they sometimes feature artisanal bakeries that aren’t listed elsewhere.

---

## 3️⃣ National & Specialty Cake Delivery Sites  

| Site | What it offers | Why use it |
|------|----------------|------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Gourmet cakes from famous bakeries across the U.S. | Great for unique flavors or iconic brands |
| **Cake Delivery** | Custom cakes delivered nationwide | You can design online, choose frosting, decorations |
| **Etsy** | Handmade cakes from independent bakers | Supports small businesses, often customizable |
| **Amazon** | Pre‑baked cakes from various sellers | Convenient if you’re already shopping there |

> **Heads‑up:** Shipping times vary; plan ahead for events or birthdays.

---

## 4️⃣ Tips for Ordering the Right Cake

| Question | What to look for |
|----------|-----------------|
| **What’s the occasion?** | Birthday → colorful, themed; Wedding → elegant, tiered |
| **Do you have dietary restrictions?** | Gluten‑free, dairy‑free, vegan, nut‑free |
| **How many people?** | Estimate servings per slice (e.g., 8 slices ≈ 12–15 guests) |
| **When do you need it?** | Order at least 24–48 hrs in advance for custom designs |
| **Budget?** | Prices range from $20–$200+ depending on size, complexity, and brand |

---

## 5️⃣ Quick Checklist Before Placing Your Order

1. **Confirm Delivery Area** – Not all shops deliver everywhere.  
2. **Ask About Customization Options** – Frosting colors, toppers, edible images.  
3. **Check Cancellation Policy** – Especially for custom orders.  
4. **Read Recent Reviews** – Look for comments on freshness, taste, and packaging.  
5. **Verify Contact Info** – Make sure you can reach the shop if anything changes.

---

### Want a Specific Recommendation?

If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated local bakeries and even suggest a few that specialize in the kind of cake you’re craving (birthday, wedding, gluten‑free, etc.). Just drop your location, and I’ll get you a curated shortlist!
